Do you see me?

Three songs about the distance between being broadcast and being known. It starts in a back room with the world turned down, and it ends in a kitchen, in person. You are the only one here. Scroll slowly.

Act I Hearing fails

Can’t Hear It

It is not indifference. It is volume: his own noise, turned up so long that everyone else went quiet underneath it. So he retreats, politely, without slamming anything.

Turned the whole world down and went to the back room.

Phone face down, headphones on, nothing playing.

Just a cleaner way to disappear.

I didn’t slam a door, I just stopped opening it.

It’s not that I don’t care.

I just can’t hear it over me.

It’s not that you’re not talking.

I just can’t hear it over me.

Woke up one morning in a life with no echo,

and realized, fuck, I’m lonely.

Not bored. Not tired. Lonely.

Neither one is true. That’s the problem.

Can you hear me in here?

I thought I was safe in here.

Act II Being seen fails

Hi Guys

He comes out of the back room the only way he knows how: on camera. Seventeen takes in, the red light is on, the ring light stays off, and the room on the other side of the lens is empty. Almost.

Live · Back room broadcast Take seventeen Stream time 00:00
Watching 0
Hi guys. Take seventeen, hi.

Chat · Comments that aren’t there yet

No one has said anything. The count says zero. Then it says one.

You
You · The one viewer · Just now

Heard. You are the only comment in the room, and it is enough.

Hi guys, do you see me now?

I couldn’t hear you from the back room.

Hi guys, do you see me now?

I came out here ’cause I had to.

Red light on and I’m sitting up straighter.

Ring light off, I look more like myself.

Glass of water I won’t drink, sitting on the shelf.

First take I smiled, deleted it.

Second take I explained too much, deleted it.

And the count says zero. Then it says one.

And I don’t know if that’s a person,

or it’s me, watching myself from the other room.

If you’re watching, say something.

If you’re not, I’ll say it anyway.

Act III Transmission ends

Last Broadcast

The red light goes off for good. The mic goes back in the drawer, the chair goes back to the table, and the question finally gets its answer: see me in person.

This is the last one. I’m not gonna dress it up.

This is the last broadcast. Then I’m getting up.

I said things in here I should’ve said in a kitchen,

to a person sitting close enough to know.

I mistook that for being known.

I mistook the hum for company, too.

This is my last broadcast.

Do you see me, do you see me now?

Not on a screen in a back room.

Just a person, just here now.

So the mic goes back in the drawer,

and the chair goes back to the table,

and the room goes back to a room,

and I go back to being reachable.

Phone charged, ringer on this time.

Door unlocked, light on in the hall.

I was never hard to love.

I was hard to reach.

Off air The broadcast is over

That’s it. I’m right here. You know where.

Come find me in person

No screen, no back room, no count in the corner. Phone charged, ringer on. Door unlocked, light on in the hall. That is the whole release plan that matters.
